newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes fall as ANS sellers withdraw.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes fall as ANS sellers withdraw.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude values fell midday Tuesday in line with lower settlement on NYMEX, while Alaska crude sellers withheld sales until they assessed shipping delays from the Port of Valdez, traders said.

BP America and Arco, key producers of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude had at least one ship each waiting at Valdez until the U.S. Coast guard would allow them to unload oily ballast water into a treatment plant, traders said.
The plant remains under investigation following the sighting of an oil slick Friday.
The sheen has officials ordering ships leaving the port to carry their ballast water since a possible culprit is a ballat-water-treatement plant at Valdez, according to officials.
This prevented ships from leaving with full loads of oil, traders said.
Meanwhile, ANS prices continued to follow NYMEX, falling to $23.52/23.72. The discount held at $1.53 under February West Texas Intermediate (WTI) following two deals January 8.
Crude traders at Texaco's Wilmington refinery were assessing if they needed to sell inventory following a early fire on one of the plant's gasoline-making units, players said.
The plant processes heavy crude oils.
A deal for Kern River heavy crude was done Monday at 15 cents under postings, traders said.
